thread:
incident-bot: ALERT: continuous-batcher queue growth detected in us-west-2-runtime pool. Multiple container restarts on gpu-rt-07, spike in 5xxs and CUDA OOMs. paging oncall

matt: i'm oncall — paging @sasha @lara. seeing repeated container exits with `cudaMemcpyAsync failed: out of memory (2)`. queue length rising fast. stack traces show batcher enqueue loops.

sasha: joining — grabbing logs now. running `kubectl logs -n runtime runtime-gpu-07 --previous` to collect crash logs.

kevin: customer-impact note: acme and stackly report ~30-50% failures on long-seq embeddings, p95 latency from ~18s -> 240s for those routes. customers also see 503s for streaming.

eng-runtime-bot: auto-analysis (quick): probable continuous-batcher growth bug triggering unbounded batch sizes when long-prefix requests intermingle with short ones. Observed metrics: `batch.size.mean` spiking to >120, `queue.length` >1k. Recommending immediate throttle: set `continuous_batcher.allow_growth=false` and `batch_growth_limit=3`.

matt: plan — 1) flip feature flag to stop growth, 2) drain the faulty node(s), 3) apply emergency revert of the auto-grow commit to 2 canaries, 4) fallback long-seq traffic to CPU-variant model. Lara can you flip the FF?

lara: flipped `runtime-config:continuous_batcher.allow_growth=false` on us-west-2 (propagated to control plane). waiting 30s for propagation, then doing a rolling restart of the daemonset on a small batch to avoid simultaneous restarts. Also increased `RUNTIME_MAX_KV_CACHE_BYTES` to 1GB temporarily to reduce paging pressure.

sasha: logs collected: repeated pattern `batcher::enqueue -> wait_on_condition -> never wake` then cuda OOM during big memcpy. attaching snippet:

```
E 2024-06-11T23:12:45Z runtime batcher.cpp:243 enqueue() waiting on condvar
E 2024-06-11T23:12:46Z runtime cuda: cudaMemcpyAsync failed: out of memory (2)
E 2024-06-11T23:12:46Z runtime containerd: restarting container runtime-pod-abc123
```

kevin: started draining gpu-rt-07: `kubectl drain gpu-rt-07 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=30`. rebalancing pods to healthy nodes. backlog estimate ~6m to clear given current throughput.

matt: deploying emergency revert (commit 9f3b2a -> previous stable) to two canaries now. will monitor for CPU and latency regressions. also routing long-seq tenants to `model-cpu-fallback` to reduce GPU pressure.

customer-success: sending notice to impacted tenants now. template: "We're experiencing degraded performance for long-context workloads in us-west-2; we're applying mitigations and will update every 10 minutes."

eng-runtime-bot: quick metric dump (pre -> post actions):
```
queue.length: 1200 -> 45
batch.size.mean: 128 -> 24
node.restarts(us-west-2): 8 -> 2
cuda.oom.count: 14 -> 1
p95.latency(target routes): 240s -> 12s
```

lara: after FF flip + canary restart, error rate falling. one node shows repeated fan-failure logs (hardware). raised ticket to infra-hw for gpu-rt-07. continuing drain for that node.

sasha: we collected core dumps from the crashed containers and uploaded to s3://redwood-incidents/1748501234/coredumps. initial grep shows `std::condition_variable` deadlock in `batch_growth_controller`.

matt: handing off to night oncall @kevin at 1748501600. current status: degraded -> stabilizing. mitigation in place: growth disabled, drains started, canary revert deployed. customer impact: partial for long-seq embedding/stream routes only. next steps:
- postmortem (owner: sasha)
- fix deadlock in batch_growth_controller and add unit/regression tests
- add circuit-breaker that rejects requests when batcher.queue > 500 and escalate
- add alerting rule for `batcher.growth_rate > 50/min` to auto-page

kevin: ack. i'll monitor for 1h and escalate if cuda.oom > 3 within 10m. enabling extended log retention: `tar -czf /tmp/runtime-logs-1748501234.tar.gz /var/log/runtime/*.log && aws s3 cp /tmp/runtime-logs-1748501234.tar.gz s3://redwood-incident-logs/1748501234.tar.gz`

lara: adding runbook update: create synthetic test that simulates long-prefix interleaving with short requests to exercise growth heuristic. will add to CI. also adding a short-circuit in runtime to cap batch size to 64 until codefix lands.

incident-bot: INCIDENT CREATED: id=INC-17485 severity=sev2 owner=matt status=investigating. next scheduled update 1748501900.

matt: todos assigned in #incidents-tracker. postmortem ETA: 3 business days. sasha volunteer to own? :thumbsup:

sasha: i'll own the postmortem and coord with infra-hw and runtime eng.

kevin: handoff note: check `cuda.oom.count` and `batch.size.mean` dashboards, watch for node flaps. escalate to eng-runtime lead if we see regressions after revert.

customer-success: customers updated at 23:30 UTC — one replied they've seen recovery and dropped error rate to ~5%. will continue updates.

matt: closing active mitigation notes in thread. retaining incident channel for postmortem coordination. thanks all.
